lines.head: Introduction
sentences: Sepsis.
What every Ambulance Officer needs to know.

lines.head: What it is
sentences: Sepsis is life threatening.
It's the body's response to an infection, damaging its own tissues and organs.
Almost any infection can cause it. The lungs, the belly, the urinary tract, or the skin.
Spot it early, treat it urgently, and you can save a life.

lines.head: The signs
sentences: So what do you look for?
Fast breathing, or breathlessness.
Fever and chills, or a low temperature.
Little or no urine.
A fast or slow heartbeat.
Confusion, or sleepiness.
And a new rash, or clammy, sweaty skin.

lines.head: First steps
sentences: Start with PPE, and basic care.
Sats under 94 percent? Give high flow oxygen.
Chronic lung disease? Call the EOC Clinician straight away about oxygen.
Use the NEWS2 calculator for every suspected infection.
And request clinical support.

lines.head: Suspected sepsis
sentences: Next, check the blood pressure.
Systolic above 100? That's suspected sepsis.
Oxygen if it's needed, and priority transport.
Consult for ongoing management.
And notify the hospital. Suspected sepsis.

lines.head: Suspected septic shock
sentences: Systolic 100 or less? That's suspected septic shock.
Request early clinical support, and use those words.
Don't let treatment hold you up. Meet your backup on the way if you need to.
High flow oxygen. Priority transport. And notify. Suspected septic shock.

lines.head: Meningococcal
sentences: Meningococcal disease can kill within hours.
Febrile, with an altered conscious state? Call the EOC Clinician about ceftriaxone.
With a rash, or without one.
The rash is a late sign. No rash doesn't rule it out.

lines.head: Ceftriaxone
sentences: If it's advised, the dose is 50 milligrams per kilogram.
The single maximum is 2 grams.
Add three and a half millilitres of saline to each 1 gram vial. That makes 4 millilitres.
Never more than 1 gram in one site.
So 2 grams means both thighs.
Allergic to cephalosporins? Consult the EOC Clinician for medical advice.

lines.head: Wrap-up
sentences: So. Spot it early.
Check the blood pressure.
Say the right words.
And get moving.
Now try the sepsis checker on this page.
